description: ADR 01214: on macOS, an iOS context that finds no managed WebDriverAgent build for the current Xcode and driver builds one into `<cacheDir>/ios/wda` before its first session, then uses it. The macOS `mobile-web-ios` CI leg restores and prebuilds no WebDriverAgent (`wdaFirstUse` in scripts/select-fixture-bundles.cjs), so on that leg the build this spec finds can only come from the run itself. The `apps-ios` leg keeps `install ios`, and so covers a run that finds a cached build and builds nothing. On Windows and Linux the toolchain probe lands the context SKIPPED. A fixture can't see the capabilities a session sends to Appium, so test/ios-installer.test.js asserts that both session builders get the managed build after a first-use build. The opt-outs (`DOC_DETECTIVE_NO_IOS_AUTOINSTALL`, `DOC_DETECTIVE_IOS_WDA_DERIVED_DATA_PATH`) and a failed build are process-wide or need a broken toolchain, so that file and test/core-core.test.js cover them too.

tests.description: Open a Safari session, which runs the iOS preflight first. Then check-managed-wda.mjs asks the session locator, in a fresh process, for the managed build. It reads the default cache directory, as the CI leg does.
